_comment: Persona dossiers transcribed by hand from public posts by researchers on X. See docs/x-dossiers.md for why this is a hand-curated file rather than a scraper source, and for the transcription rules. Every entry cites the individual post it came from. Values are re-fanged here (the source defangs them as name@gmail[.]com or drops the domain entirely); nothing else is altered, and no indicator is added that the cited post does not state. A few entries, filed under the researcher keys knowbe4, nisos and silentpush, come from a vendor's own published research or first-hand incident report rather than an X post, the rfj key carries the aliases the State Department's Rewards for Justice programme names on a reward notice, the sotahire, radenwilford and heinergarcia keys carry LinkedIn articles (and heinergarcia one Coinmonks post on Medium), the blackbigswan key also carries Ketman Project reports and the gh-fake-analyzer investigations dataset, and the meeswicky key carries a Medium post the scraper cannot reach because Medium answers it with a bot check, transcribed by hand instead. They are admitted on the same terms because they are the same kind of thing this file records: one named publisher's dated, public claim about one identity, cited to the page that made it.

Both the LinkedIn and the GitHub account were deleted after the interview. The post that carries that OSINT result was itself never cited here until 16 September 2026, and two of the accounts it shows are typeable. The LinkedIn card for Pavlo Polishichuk gives the account name pavlo-polishichuk-b68920364 and a biography in Ukrainian reading Posada Full-stack Developer u Freelancer; the post's own summary places that identity in Poland while the card places it in Shpola, Cherkasy, in Ukraine, and the card is what is recorded. The John Ruff identity is a resume hosted on bubble.io whose indexed preview carries a United States telephone number beside the highgoal215 address already held here, which is what ties the number to this persona rather than to a separate one. The Master Dev identity is a Microsoft account created on 3 November 2025 and registered to France, with only a masked telephone number shown.

dossiers.note: The researcher describes interviewing this identity as an applicant for a remote engineering role and assessing them as a North Korean IT worker. The account is presented under the name Ming Cheng. The thread notes a three-year gap in the resume covering 2018 to 2021, which the applicant explained as COVID-19 treatment beginning in 2019, months before the virus was known in China, and says the interview was cut short by a connection problem shortly after the applicant was asked whether he was North Korean. The third post of that thread publishes the whole application under the heading "all the fake details he applied with for anyone tracking", and is where the address, telephone number, GitHub, Telegram, IP address and website here come from. It was missed on the first pass: X renders a post that long behind a Show more control, and the syndication endpoint the reader uses returns it truncated and says so. It has to be read in a browser. That post also attributes the GitHub account to the Contagious Trader campaign, weaponised cryptocurrency trading bots, citing kmsec's write-up, which is already a source here; this entry carries that label alongside IT Worker Fraud because the researcher makes both claims. This is a second, independent researcher reaching the same conclusion about an identity the lazarus.group registry already records, so the account carries both citations. Two days after the thread that named this operator, the researcher reported that it had rotated to a new persona, 0xcrypoops, and gave the replacement X, GitHub and Telegram accounts. The three are recorded here rather than as a separate persona because the source states outright that they are the same operator continuing. Note that the Telegram handle for the replacement is not a copy of the other two: it begins with the letter o where the X and GitHub handles begin with a zero, and it is transcribed as the post links it.

unattributed.note: A self-thread the researcher tags #DPRK #KONNI, describing an invitation to a fake Sanctum and Superteam Korea event during Korea Blockchain Week in Seoul. The LNK runs conhost and PowerShell, carves a decoy PDF and an XOR-encoded payload out of itself, writes the payload to a .err file under C:\ProgramData\Diagnosis and registers a scheduled task that runs a PowerShell backdoor every 30 minutes, falling back to SYSTEM. The backdoor talks to a PHP endpoint on an InfinityFree subdomain and exits if any of 53 analysis tools is running. The four hashes are, in order, the ZIP, the .err payload, the PowerShell script and the decoy PDF, as the thread labels them; the decoy is the lure document itself, not malicious code.

unattributed.label: Bitget theft: second attacker distribution wallet
unattributed.note: TRM Labs' analysis of the Bitget hot-wallet theft of 24 September 2026 names this as the second Ethereum wallet the stolen funds passed through, which distributed its balance to newly created wallets over about two hours; the first, 0x770b10b273fc44fe9197d6bf20f145c2e98463ee, is on Bitget's own list of attacker receiving addresses. The scraper read the report but the sentence carries none of the words its wallet guard requires, so the address is recorded here. TRM called the attribution likely but not definitive; Chainalysis attributed the theft to DPRK actors on 1 October 2026 (https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/387m-bitget-theft-2026).
